text: **Work Summary – Lucas Petit, Cryptographer**  This quarter, my focus centered on advancing post-quantum cryptographic implementations and auditing existing key management protocols. I completed the integration of CRYSTALS-Kyber into our internal messaging layer, replacing the previous elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman handshake. Performance benchmarks show a 14% latency increase, which I mitigated by introducing batch precomputation of polynomial coefficients for ephemeral keys.  I also led a security review of the threshold signature scheme used in our custody service. Through formal verification with EasyCrypt, I identified a flaw in the nonce generation step that could allow a malicious minority to bias the final signature. I patched the protocol by adding a commit-reveal round, then ran a full test suite of 2,000 randomized trials to confirm correctness. The fix will be deployed in version 2.3.1.  On the research side, I drafted a proposal for a lattice-based zero-knowledge range proof, aimed at reducing proof size by 30% compared to Bulletproofs. I have implemented a prototype in Rust and am currently evaluating its soundness under the Module-SIS assumption. Preliminary results are encouraging, but I need to verify edge cases involving high-bit overflow.  Collaboration with the engineering team improved after I created a decision tree for selecting hash functions based on security level and hardware constraints. This document has already reduced onboarding time for new developers. I also reviewed six external pull requests related to randomness generation, fixing two instances of non-constant-time comparison.  Looking ahead, I plan to finalize the range proof paper, audit the new key derivation function against side-channel attacks, and begin integration testing with our hardware security module.
